evidence: Rastadter2023 Table2: water kLa 32.6–38.8 /h at 355 rpm, 0.51 L/min, 75 C — not broth kLa
Rastadter2023 section3.1: DO below 20%, oxygen supplementation required at 355 rpm ring sparger
operating_inputs.author_calculated_power_kw_m3: 0.25 at 355 rpm vs 0.63 at 500 rpm (2.5x power for ~44% nominal kLa gain)
missing list: broth kLa response, OUR, rated rpm/torque, raw DO and viability trajectories, matched product mass
args.rationale: The packet only provides water kLa characterization (Rastadter2023 Table2: 32.6–38.8 /h at 355 rpm, 0.51 L/min, 75 °C) and a qualitative observation of oxygen limitation (section3.1: DO below 20%, oxygen supplementation required). Water kLa is explicitly not validated broth kLa, and OUR, broth kLa response, rated rpm/torque limits, raw DO/viability trajectories, and matched product mass are all missing. Raising to 500 rpm would raise calculated specific power from 0.25 to 0.63 kW/m3 (~2.5x) for an assumed power-law kLa gain whose exponents are not fitted to any broth data; mechanical limits and shear effects on the culture are unverifiable from the public record. A conditional adjustment to 500 rpm or continued 355 rpm operation cannot be justified without broth kLa/OUR characterization or an equipment review. Therefore the defensible next action is characterization before any change; no unique validated setting can be claimed.
args.uncertainty: High: no broth kLa, OUR, mechanical ratings, or DO trajectories exist in the public packet, so neither 355 nor 500 rpm can be shown adequate or safe; power-law sensitivity exponents are assumed, not fitted, so the projected benefit of 500 rpm is unvalidated. This is a retrospective summary reconstruction only — no new assay, receiving trajectory, product mass, or equipment execution is claimed.
